briefing.opening: Good morning. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 22, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Unprecedented Deepening of the Climate Crisis and Widespread Impacts
sections.content: Today's briefing underscores the overwhelming reality of the intensifying global climate crisis. The recent 'jaw-dropping' El Niño phenomenon has far surpassed its anticipated peak, breaking historical temperature records [89, 91]. This aligns with scientists' warnings that seven of the nine 'planetary boundaries' essential for Earth's life-support systems have been breached to unprecedented levels [88]. These unparalleled climate changes are having widespread global impacts, including potato shortages in Europe due to extreme heatwaves and droughts [8], an increased risk of deadly landslides in Alaska [50], wildfires destroying wildlife habitats in the UK [90], and intensifying flood disasters in the Himalayas and Nepal regions [73, 74]. Domestically, the climate crisis has disrupted the water cycle, leading to simultaneous floods and droughts [6], once again highlighting the urgent need for immediate and decisive action on climate change [62].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges in Climate Policy and Negative Trends
sections.content: Despite efforts to address the climate crisis, climate change denial statements and policy setbacks by some political leaders are causing concern. Former U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed global warming is a 'hoax' [10, 12, 54, 56, 81], and the federal government's easing of climate change regulations for power plants in Indiana [53] reflects this negative trend. Domestically, issues such as the prevalence of shell companies and alleged collusion in local government evaluations within renewable energy convergence support projects [29, 39] have raised questions about the transparency and efficiency of policy implementation. Furthermore, the blocking of New York State's Climate Change Superfund Act by a judge [65] illustrates the ongoing difficulty in securing legal and policy momentum for climate action.

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Expanding Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: On a positive note, global renewable energy generation has set new records [45], and domestic and international companies are actively working towards their carbon neutrality goals. The number of companies participating in 'The Climate Pledge' has surpassed 700, accelerating towards a net-zero target by 2040 [11]. Hyundai Motor supported carbon neutrality efforts by supplying eco-friendly electric buses to Morocco [13]. Several local governments in Korea are also implementing proactive carbon neutrality policies. Gwangmyeong City is accelerating its transition to a carbon-neutral city by providing additional support for 351 electric vehicles [15, 21, 25, 27], and Siheung City is strengthening its RE100 response capabilities through lectures on renewable energy transition [20, 22, 38, 41]. Furthermore, five power generation companies plan to collectively quadruple their renewable energy production by 2030 [31], and Gangjin County is soliciting community-led renewable energy participation villages [43], demonstrating positive changes where rural renewable energy expands to increase farm income and energy independence [30]. In addition, it is encouraging to hear that despite this summer's heatwave, the incidence of high-concentration ozone nationwide decreased, marking the second-lowest number of ozone advisories since 2016 [49].

sections.title: 🌍 The New Intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Climate Action
sections.content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a double-edged sword in addressing climate change. Türkiye, the host country for COP31, launched an AI climate initiative ahead of the upcoming summit [83, 92], suggesting that AI could be a crucial tool for solving the climate crisis [75]. However, simultaneously, the UN climate chief called for greater scrutiny of AI's immense energy consumption [82], and discussions at Climate Week focused on balancing 'hope for clean energy and uncertainty about artificial intelligence' [51, 61]. These discussions present the complex challenge of managing the potential risks of AI technology as a new source of carbon emissions, even as it contributes to achieving climate goals.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Efforts to Raise Climate Change Awareness and Adaptation
sections.content: Domestically, efforts to raise awareness and adapt to climate change are continuously underway. Chungju City has a special lecture scheduled on the theme of 'Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality' [2], and various local governments, including Suwon City and Siheung City, are strengthening the capabilities of public officials and citizens through customized carbon neutrality practice education and renewable energy transition lectures [20, 22, 23, 41]. Seongdong-gu is showcasing specific regional adaptation examples, such as creating a sustainable garden called 'Seongdong's Seasons' in response to climate change [4, 5]. The Yongin Special City Council is also seeking solutions by holding policy discussions on carbon neutrality through a circular economy [17, 26]. Regulatory changes due to ESG and carbon neutrality policies are being discussed in the construction and real estate industries [14], and the introduction of renewable energy is included in the labor-management negotiations at GM Korea [44], indicating that climate change response is becoming a major agenda across society. This demonstrates the importance of citizen participation and institutional improvement in an era of climate crisis [19, 69].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the coexistence of hopeful changes and policy challenges amidst an unprecedented climate crisis. We must acknowledge the scientific realities of climate change and strive to build a sustainable future through global cooperation and action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
